result.title: From Diagnosing Alignment to Joint Supervision in Multimodal Draft Training
result.summary: Multimodal drafts learn from multimodal (MM) and text-only (TXT) supervision, yet their effects on alignment and how to combine them remain unclear. We diagnose draft-target alignment through paired predictions with and without visual input, decomposing distributional error into text-conditioned and visual-response components. Drafts with similar text-conditioned alignment can still differ markedly in visual-response risk and acceptance. Controlled continuation training shows that high-risk groups outperform random and low-risk groups, and visual-response risk guides MM training more effectively than aggregate risk. Building on these diagnostics, we propose MNRS-Joint, which configures joint supervision from a given draft's component-risk distributions, using modality-specific mean risks to determine the MM:TXT mixture. Across three warm-ups, its distinct mixtures fall in high-performing regions of the ratio sweeps. On LLaVA-1.5-7B, MNRS-Joint improves mean accepted length from 3.35 to 3.53 and mean speedup from $2.04\times$ to $2.16\times$ over composition-matched random training under greedy tree decoding. The gains also hold under stochastic chain decoding.

AI.brief_summary: 该文诊断多模态草稿模型与目标模型的对齐，利用有无视觉输入的成对预测分解误差，并据此提出 MNRS-Joint，按模态风险配置多模态与纯文本监督比例，以提升推测解码的接受长度和加速比。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「有无视觉输入」的成对误差分解和视觉响应风险，可能为核查 VLM 推理中的视觉旁路及视觉/文本监督贡献提供方法线索；但论文目标是解码效率，并非 latent 推理状态本身。
